newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Maracaibo pilots drop strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Maracaibo pilots drop strike threat.

text.p: Lake Maracaibo shipping pilots have agreed to drop a strike threat after the Venezuelan government agreed to tighten oil tanker draught limits on a channel that has seen three groundings in the past two months, pilots said.
The strike was to begin Monday over pilots requests that the draught limit be tightened to 36 feet to prevent further groundings in the silted channel.
But after meeting with Transport Ministry officials Thursday the pilots agreed to waive the threat with one condition -- that the National Guard stopped harassing them.
"If we don't get a firm reply (on this) by Monday, we'll reintroduce the strike threat," pilots representative Fidel Sanchez told Reuters.
"But I believe the problem will be resolved and we'll keep on working," he said.
The draught limit will remain in place while dredging continues, Sanchez said. Some 70 percent of Venezuelan exports pass through the channel into the Venezuelan Gulf.
